decisions.decision: Deadlines live in an optional ticket field in the version-1 file, which 1.4.0 drops when it writes, so preserving the original deadlines on re-upgrade relies on operators keeping a pre-rollback copy and recovering the deadlines from it while retaining updates made under 1.4.0.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a return to the new release to recover assigned deadlines automatically after 1.4.0 has written ticket updates.

decisions.decision: With DUE_TIMES=on, the service refuses to start if an existing data file is missing any ticket deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the service to keep answering in legacy mode and warn operators until the file is ready.

decisions.decision: An invalid response-hours override causes configuration to fail and the error names the variable.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the service to start with the default hours for that priority and log a warning.

decisions.decision: The new release assigns a deadline when a ticket is created even with DUE_TIMES off, with the switch controlling when the deadline is exposed.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted tickets created during the disabled rollout window to receive their deadlines in the backfill immediately before activation.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9, 13, 25 (R-1, R-2 and R-5) and record/03-research.md:16

decisions.decision: The backfill uses each legacy ticket's priority as stored at migration time to calculate its deadline from its creation timestamp.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the priority at creation, recoverable from the ticket's audit history, to determine the deadline for a ticket whose priority has since changed.

decisions.decision: Delivery ends with the local source changes and rollout instructions, and operations owns the production migration and switch.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the work to include coordinating the production migration and activation with operations.

decisions.decision: With overdue=true, a ticket must be overdue and still match the existing status-or-priority group when both filters are supplied.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a ticket to satisfy both supplied filters as well as the overdue check, matching the API documentation's description of combined filters.

decisions.decision: The overdue filter runs before cursor pagination, so the page limit and next cursor are based on matching tickets.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the overdue filter applied within each ordinary ticket page so the page boundaries stay aligned with the unfiltered list.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13 (R-2 Enabled ticket views and overdue listing)

decisions.decision: Enabling due times adds the deadline to the human-facing CLI views while keeping the four-column list --raw output used by the weekly report.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted an opt-in raw column so scripts can read deadlines while existing report invocations keep their four-column output.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13, 29 (R-2 and Non-functional requirements) and repo/README.md:70–72

decisions.decision: With due times enabled, values of the overdue parameter other than true leave the ticket listing unfiltered by deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted unsupported values to return a validation error so mistyped filters cannot silently produce a broader list.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:13 (R-2 Enabled ticket views and overdue listing)

decisions.decision: Backfilling deadlines preserves the audit log and outbox as they were.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the backfill to append an audit entry for each deadline it assigned.

decisions.decision: The due field uses an ISO timestamp in UTC.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted due represented as a numeric Unix timestamp.
